newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says it trusts German justice over fires.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says it trusts German justice over fires.

text.p: Turkey said on Friday it had faith in German justice in dealing with arson attacks against Turks but expressed concern that recent fires in Turkish homes in Holland and Germany may spawn racist attacks.
"We have confidence in the German police," Turkish foreign ministry undersecretary Onur Oymen told foreign reporters. "We have nothing to complain of in German justice so far."
German police said earlier they had detained the father of a Turkish family on suspicion he started a fire on Sunday in the town of Krefeld in which his wife and two children died.
On Thursday the German government summoned Turkey's ambassador to protest at criticism from Ankara suggesting that Germany was not doing enough to protect immigrants.
The semi-official Anatolian news agency quoted Turkey's Interior Minister Meral Aksener as saying on Thursday that "they (Germans) couldn't throw us out, now they are trying to burn us out".

Oymen denied that any Turkish officials had accused Germany of not doing enough. "As far as I know no Turkish politician has accused the German government," he said. "I do not believe the minister said such a thing because this is not our policy. Probably it was misreporting."
Oymen said he was concerned that arson incidents in Germany and Holland this week could be a catalyst for neo-Nazi attacks.

"I urge the Dutch and the Germans to protect the Turks," he said. "It may well not be a neo-Nazi attack in Krefeld, but we may have similar attacks...It is like a contagious disease -- one month after Solingen there were 75 attacks against Turks."

Five members of a Turkish family died in a racist arson attack in the German town of Solingen in 1993. Four Germans were sentenced to between 10-15 years in prison on counts of murder, attempted murder and arson.
On Tuesday, a Turkish man was injured after a fire at his home in the German town of Haigerseelbach. Investigators were not ruling out the possibility of a racist attack, police said.
Six members of a Turkish immigrant family died in the Netherlands last week in an arson attack being investigated amid suspicions that it may have been motivated by racial hatred.
Turkey's relations with Europe have been strained in recent months by Turkish frustrations at a perceived lack of progress in its bid to become a full member of the European Union.
